items.text: Among adults starting the group pain self-management programme in 2027, does introducing an orientation call and a hybrid video option, then an evening group if approved, increase reach and the proportion completing six or more sessions compared with the 2025 to 2026 baseline, and for whom?
items.intervention: Orientation call, hybrid video option and, if approved, an evening group, introduced in sequence
items.comparator: Baseline cohorts from the previous 18 months
items.outcome: Completion of six or more sessions; reach among referred people
items.time: Each eight-week group and three months after

items.text: Why do people leave the programme early, and how do the adaptations change their experience?
items.population: People who leave early and people who complete
items.intervention: Experience of attending the standard and adapted programme
items.outcome: Reasons for leaving and experience of adaptations, mapped to CFIR constructs

finer: Feasible within existing staff time for the orientation call and hybrid option; interesting to the clinic and people on the waiting list; novel locally; ethical with consent for follow-up contact; relevant because the waiting list depends on completion.
summary: One implementation outcome question and one question about reasons for leaving.
